page: Amazon Web Services h1.2xlarge is a first-generation storage-optimized instance engineered for data-intensive applications requiring large volumes of cost-effective local magnetic storage. Powered by a 2.3 GHz Intel Xeon E5-2686 v4 processor built on the x86_64 architecture, the instance provides 8 dedicated vCPUs across 4 physical cores with 2 threads per core. System memory is sized at 32.0 GB, yielding a balanced 4.0 GB of memory per core. A key feature of the configuration is its bundled 2000 GB local hard disk drive (HDD). The instance is virtualized on the Xen hypervisor, provides a baseline network throughput of 2 Gbps, and contains no hardware GPU accelerators.

Synthetic benchmark evaluations reflect the architectural constraints of the older Intel Broadwell CPU generation. Single-core performance falls in the lower tiers, with a stress-ng score of 883.18 and a Geekbench single-core score of 904.0. Multi-threaded metrics follow a similar pattern, recording 4177.44 on stress-ng and 3371.0 on Geekbench multi-core. PassMark CPU execution reached 6218.11, while its memory score held in the average tier at 1968.21. Memory bandwidth tests measure 38.02 GB/sec for uncached read operations and 22.65 GB/sec for uncached writes. Throughput metrics record static web serving at 5.36 GB/sec and Redis key operations at 2.51 million operations per second.

From a cost and architectural perspective, h1.2xlarge trades high-speed compute and ultra-low random I/O latency for dense local storage capacity. The inclusion of a 2 TB mechanical drive provides significant block storage capacity without incurring separate network-attached storage volume overhead. However, workloads requiring intensive vector processing or modern instruction sets are limited by the absence of AVX-512 extensions. The hardware profile aligns closely with sequential file processing, Apache Hadoop or MapReduce data nodes, log aggregation repositories, bulk data archiving, and legacy batch extract-transform-load (ETL) pipelines.
